title: VisAlign: Mitigating Hallucinations via Refining Textual Embeddings
description: Investigated text-embedding space refinement in the Qwen2-VL architecture to enhance visual grounding and reduce hallucinations.

details.Problem: Large vision language models tend to over rely on language tokens because visual embeddings are simply appended to the text stream, which leads to weak visual grounding and hallucination.
details.What I did: Implemented the VisAlign refinement in the OpenQwen2VL stack and ran the full pretraining and evaluations. Integrated average pooled visual features into textual embeddings at inference, executed experiments, and prepared the result tables and plots for the paper.
details.Impact and Results: Integrated VisAlign into OpenQwen2VL and ran full pretraining plus eval scripts. Preliminary benchmarks suggest lower hallucination rates with improved grounding; full OpenQwen2VL numbers pending. (Published in ACL Findings, 2026)

title: Frames2LoRA: Parametric Video Internalization for Vision-Language Models
description: Introduced Frames2LoRA, a method for parametric video internalization where a perceiver hypernetwork generates a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapter directly from a video's intermediate representations in a single forward pass, enabling video question answering and summarization with zero visual tokens at query time.

details.Problem: Video reasoning in VLMs is extremely token-heavy, causing high latency, large context window usage, and context degeneration during long-video question answering.
details.What I did: Introduced Frames2LoRA, a method for parametric video internalization. Designed a perceiver hypernetwork that runs layer-by-layer alongside a frozen VLM to ingest intermediate video representations and predict Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) weight adapters in a single forward pass, entirely bypassing iterative gradient-based training. Implemented training on SmolVLM2 (500M and 2.2B) for video question answering, summarization, and captioning.
details.Impact and Results: Reduces query-time visual tokens by 1500x and TTFT by up to 80x while maintaining accuracy. (Under Review at EMNLP, 2026)

title: The Low-Frequency Trap: Video–Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
description: Introduced trace-grounded parametric profiling for video-language models, generating 2,190 controlled videos with executable ground-truth traces across event count N and frequency F grid sweeps to audit model reasoning and diagnose temporal failure modes.

details.Problem: Standard video benchmarks use fixed clips that entangle event count, rate, duration, and visual clutter, while existing programmatic benchmarks score only final answers without auditing intermediate temporal traces against ground truth.
details.What I did: Developed a trace-grounded parametric profiling framework for event counting across three controlled video tasks (Bouncing Ball wall contacts, visual blinks, categorical state transitions) paired with executable event traces across 2,190 synthetic videos. Audited model-reported timestamps (precision, recall, trace F1, ACR, RFR) for Gemini 3.6 Flash, Qwen3-VL-235B, and GPT-5.6 Sol under sampling density sweeps (1–16 FPS), oracle keyframe evidence, and prompting interventions.
details.Impact and Results: Exposed a staged temporal failure and the low-frequency trap, showing models recover only 18.1% of true events under high temporal load. Demonstrated that increasing sampling density (1–16 FPS) inflates final integer counts without producing faithful step-by-step trace agreement (trace F1 remains near 3.7%). (Under Review at AAAI, 2027)

title: PlanForge: Executable Planner Generation from Natural Language
description: Developed an Architect–Builder–Runner framework that converts natural-language planning problems into executable solver programs rather than direct textual plans.

details.Problem: Traditional direct LLM plan generation from natural language is highly brittle, unverified, and generalizes poorly to multi-constraint tasks with multiple valid solutions.
details.Architecture and Workflow: Architect Stage: Infers state representations, function decompositions, algorithmic strategies, and verification logic from natural-language planning problems without a fixed schema or prescribed search algorithm. Builder Pipeline: Converts solver designs into executable code, including parsing, constraint checking, search/solving logic, helper functions, and iterative code–test–fix repair. Runner Execution: Implements a deterministic runner that executes generated solvers and accepts only verified outputs: a valid executable plan, a no-plan verdict for unreachable goals, or a failure signal.
details.Impact and Results: Evaluated PlanForge on ACPBench, Tower of Hanoi, Frogs Jumping, and NaturalPlan, showing vastly improved execution-grounded planning over direct LLM plan generation. Achieved a 100% success rate on NaturalPlan trip planning, meeting planning, and calendar scheduling, demonstrating flawless transfer to multi-constraint planning tasks with multiple valid solutions. (Under Review at AAAI, 2027)

title: Multi-Step Reasoning Using Process Reward Models
description: Evaluated process supervision in mathematical reasoning by training step-level Process Reward Models (PRMs) versus outcome-only verifiers.

details.Problem: Outcome-only supervision in math reasoning rewards the final answer but ignores the quality of intermediate steps. This leads to brittle chains of thought, unnecessarily long solutions, and failures that are hard to diagnose or correct. Our hypothesis is that using PRM would produce more correct steps.
details.What I built: An end-to-end PRM pipeline that generates multi-step trajectories, assigns weak step-level labels using verifier/self-consistency signals, and uses that score at inference for PRM-guided answers.
details.Impact and Results: Experimenting on GSM8K PRM guidance underperformed both baselines across held out sets. Our initial results demonstrates that Majority voting was consistently strongest with a 92% accuracy compared to PRM with a 68% accuracy.

title: Large Language Models for Code Deobfuscation
description: Automated LLVM-IR low-level deobfuscation under Bogus Control Flow (BCF) and Control Flow Flattening (CFF) using reasoner LLMs.

details.Problem: Automating deobfuscation of low level LLVM-IR is difficult with existing tools that struggle under Bogus Control Flow and Control Flow Flattening, and there is no standardized AI evaluation for this setting.
details.What I did: Led the AI modeling and evaluation track. Designed Chain of Thought procedural prompts with global variable tracing. Built an LLVM-IR analysis module to extract basic blocks and control flow graphs and to compute Cyclomatic Complexity and instruction counts. Implemented an adjustment step to normalize identifiers for fair Levenshtein similarity. Created an evaluation harness using Code Reduction, Levenshtein Similarity, and Cyclomatic Complexity and benchmarked four reasoner models on O-LLVM obfuscations.
details.Impact and Results: Established a 36 sample LLVM-IR benchmark across BCF, CFF, and BCF-CFF. Best model achieved 76.9% code reduction and 85% similarity on BCF-CFF with Cyclomatic Complexity reduced from 91 to 13.5 (85%). (Published at WoRMA, 2026)

title: CPER: From Guessing to Asking (Persona Knowledge Gap Resolution)
description: Developed CPER, a three-module dialogue system that identifies knowledge gaps and asks targeted questions to align with a user's dynamic persona.

details.Problem: Large language models in multi-turn chats miss user-specific context, creating a persona knowledge gap that leads to generic, incoherent, or misaligned replies.
details.What I did: Designed CPER, a three-module framework that quantifies uncertainty, asks targeted clarifying questions, and generates persona-aligned responses. Implemented and evaluated on CCPE-M and ESConv.
details.Impact and Results: Human A/B judges preferred CPER over strong baselines by +42% on CCPE-M and +27% on ESConv, with strongest gains in long (12+ turn) conversations; GPT-4o preference on CCPE-M reached 60.78%. (Published at NAACL 2025 SRW)

title: Automated Planning and Code Synthesis for Continual ML Ideation
description: Developed an LLM-driven planning and code-generation system to automate the mining and execution of ML research ideas from papers.

details.Problem: Turning new research ideas into runnable changes in an existing ML pipeline is slow and inconsistent. Teams need automatic extraction of ideas from papers and automatic plan to code execution with minimal manual effort.
details.What was built: An LLM driven system that mines techniques and goals from a set of papers with a RAG workflow, then produces a modification plan, and generates, debugs, and finalizes code.
details.Impact and Results: Internal runs showed about a 30% increase in executable code yield from optimized prompting and iterative repair, and successful end to end execution of planned modifications with minimal manual intervention.

title: Multimodal RAG Chatbot with Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
description: Shipped an enterprise-grade multimodal RAG chatbot integrating custom MCP server endpoints for secure internal system queries and conversational clarification.

details.Problem: Enterprise customers need to retrieve grounded information across mixed PDFs, diagrams, and tables, as well as seamlessly execute dynamic actions on external APIs and databases without high UI friction.
details.What I built: Designed and shipped a multimodal RAG chatbot processing text, images, and tables with precise intent verification. Integrated custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers enabling chat-driven database query execution, semantic search, and system status synchronization. Added a clarification step based on my multi-turn LLM research to improve intent capture.
details.Impact and Results: Deployed the chatbot securely for active enterprise clients at IPCA and Taj, reducing manual task overhead by over 30% and significantly enhancing search accuracy.

title: Computer Vision Duplicate Bill Identification System
description: Built an AI duplicate invoice identification pipeline using OCR text parsing and CLIP multimodal embeddings.

details.Problem: Corporate financial audits lose significant capital to duplicate bill invoicing and fraud due to subtle visual and textual duplicate matches.
details.What I built: Developed an AI-powered duplicate bill identification system combining OCR text extraction and CLIP visual embeddings to compare and match invoice duplicates.
details.Impact and Results: Deployed a working prototype in Streamlit, achieving 95% identification accuracy and substantially reducing auditing friction for finance teams.

title: RAG-based Resume Matching & Classification Pipeline
description: Developed an automated candidate-to-job matching solution using LangChain, Ollama, and FAISS vector indices.

details.Problem: Recruitment teams waste significant hours manually parsing and classifying unstructured resumes against complex job descriptions.
details.What I built: Designed a RAG-based resume matching and scoring pipeline using LangChain, Ollama (Llama 3), and FAISS vector databases to align and index applicant skills.
details.Impact and Results: Streamlined HR screening workflows, reducing manual review efforts by 40% with functional Streamlit prototypes.
